ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Hint: Please answer the question requiring an integer answer and provide the final value, e.g., 1, 2, 3, at the end.
Question: In the <image>, the logic gates shown in the digital circuit below use strong pull-down nMOS transistors for LOW logic level at the outputs. When the pull-downs are off, high-value resistors set the output logic levels to HIGH (i.e., the pull-ups are weak). Note that some nodes are intentionally shorted to implement "wired logic." Such shorted nodes will be HIGH only if the outputs of all the gates whose outputs are shorted are HIGH.
The number of distinct values of \( X_3X_2X_1X_0 \) (out of the 16 possible values) that give \( Y = 1 \) is ______.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The inputs in the diagram are X0, X1, X2, and X3. X1 and X2 enter an XOR gate, and its output is connected at the same node with the output of X3 after passing through an inverter, forming the first intentionally shorted wired-logic node. X0 enters an inverter along one path and directly enters an AND gate along another path; the other input of this AND gate comes from the first shorted node. The AND gate output is also shorted with the output of the X0 inverter, forming the second wired-logic node, and serves as the upper input of the final OR gate. X3 is also directly connected to the lower input of the final OR gate, and the OR gate output is Y. Reasoning: Since a shorted node is HIGH only when all gate outputs shorted to that node are HIGH, the first shorted node is equivalent to A = (X1 ⊕ X2) · ¬X3. The AND gate output is B = X0 · A. The second shorted node is equivalent to C = ¬X0 · B = ¬X0 · X0 · A = 0. Therefore the final output Y = C + X3 = 0 + X3 = X3. So Y=1 if and only if X3=1. At this time X2, X1, and X0 may take arbitrary values, for a total of 2^3 = 8 kinds.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit connections visible in the image: identify the two intentional shorted nodes, one between the XOR(X1,X2) output and NOT(X3), and one between NOT(X0) and the output of an AND gate whose inputs are X0 and the first shorted node. Translate these into equations. Let A=(X1⊕X2)·¬X3 for the lower shorted node. The AND output is B=X0·A. The upper shorted node feeding the final OR is C=¬X0·B=¬X0·X0·A=0. Since the lower input of the final OR is the direct X3 line, Y=C+X3=X3. Therefore exactly the 8 input words with X3=1 give Y=1.
